payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image provide enough evidence to determine whether the paper has been stuffed into the cup?
node.criteria: Pass if the image clearly resolves whether the paper is inside the cup and stuffed into it. Fail if the image clearly shows it is not stuffed into the cup. Unknown if visibility or ambiguity prevents a determination; retain this as unresolved rather than inferring completion or absence.
node.binding: Use only visible evidence of the paper’s placement relative to the cup; do not treat proximity or contact with the rim alone as proof of stuffing.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image clearly shows the paper held outside the cup, not inside or stuffed into it, so the placement can be determined. The cup is partly obscured, but the paper is visibly separate from it.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image shows a hand holding the paper near the cup, but the paper is not visibly inside or stuffed into it.

fulfillment: The current binding is truncated/ambiguous and omits the source-to-edit comparison, while the node’s fuller criteria correctly distinguish absent from partial progress. Preserve that distinction: assess whether the requested paper-to-cup placement changed relative to the source, and count only observable progress toward putting the paper into the cup—not unrelated edits or mere proximity. Here the edited image shows a hand holding a blue card-like object, with no visible cup; the source shows a white paper and blue cup. This supports no evidenced progress, but the missing/changed objects make the target comparison less secure than the traces’ high confidence suggests. Ensure the node can return unknown when the target objects or their relation cannot be reliably identified, rather than treating an unobservable target as confidently absent. The checks executed successfully, so this is a visual-evidence/binding issue, not a transport or dependency failure.
